name: BLIND HUGHIE
description: Blind Hughie is a lighthearted domino variant where players must match tiles without knowing what they hold. Each participant keeps their tiles in a face-down row and can only flip the rightmost tile on their turn. If it matches the central line, it is played; otherwise, it is returned face-down to the left end of the row. It is a game of high luck and social energy, where a sharp memory provides the only strategic edge as tiles cycle back through the player's row.

content.text: Blind Hughie is a lighthearted domino variant where players must match tiles without knowing what they hold. Each participant keeps their tiles in a face-down row and can only flip the rightmost tile on their turn. If it matches the central line, it is played; otherwise, it is returned face-down to the left end of the row. It is a game of high luck and social energy, where a sharp memory provides the only strategic edge as tiles cycle back through the player's row.

Originating as a casual variation of the standard Block domino game, Blind Hughie was developed to simplify the strategy and increase the element of surprise. It is a traditional Western folk game with long-standing popularity in English-speaking card rooms and Dutch cafes (where it is known as Billitonnen).
Players draw tiles based on player count (2p=7, 3p=5, 4p=5). Tiles are placed in a face-down row in front of each player. No one may look at their cards.

items.text: Billitonnen: The Dutch variant where the leftmost tile is flipped instead of the rightmost.
